record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: In the same setting for U_α, is every boundary point x ∈ ∂U_α accessible both from within U_α and from the complement of U_α?

evidence.quote: Nothing is known (e.g. is every point x ∈ ∂Uα accessible from Uα and the exterior of Uα ?).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f: A → A be a smooth area-preserving twist diffeomorphism of the closed annulus A = S^1 × [0,1] (or, equivalently, consider the standard family of area-preserving twist maps depending on a parameter α). For an irrational number α satisfying a Diophantine condition, KAM theory guarantees the existence of an f-invariant essential closed curve on which the dynamics is smoothly conjugate to the rigid rotation by α. Define
   U_α = the union of all f-invariant essential closed curves on which f is smoothly conjugate to rotation by α-Diophantine rotation numbers (the "KAM set"),
viewed as a subset of A, and let ∂U_α be its topological boundary in A.

Question: Is every boundary point x ∈ ∂U_α accessible both from inside U_α and from the complement A \ U_α? That is, for each x ∈ ∂U_α, do there exist continuous arcs γ_1: [0,1] → A and γ_2: [0,1] → A with γ_1(1) = γ_2(1) = x, γ_1([0,1)) ⊂ U_α, and γ_2([0,1)) ⊂ A \ U_α?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not return any published result resolving the accessibility of boundary points of the KAM set U_α from either side. The original framing explicitly states that "nothing is known" about this question, and no subsequent literature found in the search establishes accessibility (or inaccessibility) of ∂U_α from U_α and from its exterior. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: KAM approach to outer billiards (Kosenko)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses KAM invariant curves and boundary structure of regions filled by KAM curves, without resolving accessibility of boundary points.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the KAM boundary accessibility question is given in available literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: Accessible and Inaccessible Basin Boundary Points
status_evidence.snippet: General discussion of accessible/inaccessible boundary points in dynamical systems; does not address the KAM set U_α specifically.
status_evidence.claim: The notion of accessibility of boundary points is studied in dynamics, but no specific result for the KAM boundary is reported.
